evidence.title: LeBlanc A, et al. Bone mineral and lean tissue loss after long duration space flight. J Musculoskelet Neuronal Interact. 2000;1(2):157–160.
evidence.excerpt: Crew members on 4–14.4 month missions lost bone mineral density at an average of roughly 1–1.5% per month in the spine and hip, with the largest losses in weight-bearing regions.

evidence.title: Gabel L, et al. Incomplete recovery of bone strength and trabecular microarchitecture at the distal tibia 1 year after return from long duration spaceflight. Sci Rep. 2022;12:9446.
evidence.excerpt: High-resolution scans of 17 astronauts found tibial bone strength and density were only partly recovered one year after return, with longer missions associated with less recovery.

evidence.title: Vico L, Hargens A. Skeletal changes during and after spaceflight. Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2018;14:229–245.
evidence.excerpt: A review of skeletal adaptation to microgravity: bone loss concentrates in the lower limbs and spine, countermeasures such as resistive exercise reduce but do not remove it.
